Let \( A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots \) be a sequence of finite nonempty sets of positive integers. Given that \( |A_i \cap A_j| = \gcd(i, j) \) for all (not necessarily distinct) positive integers \( i \) and \( j \), compute the minimum possible value of

\[
\sum_{d|250} \max A_d,
\]

where the sum ranges over all positive integer divisors \( d \) of 250.

(For a finite nonempty set \( S \), we define \( \max S \) as the largest element of \( S \).)


Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
We will first determine the exact structure of any sequence satisfying the condition, then reduce the problem to an optimization on the divisors of \(250\).

---

## 1. Structure of the family \((A_i)\)

Taking \(i=j\), we get

\[
|A_i|=\gcd(i,i)=i.
\]

If \(m\mid n\), then

\[
|A_m\cap A_n|=\gcd(m,n)=m=|A_m|,
\]

so

\[
A_m\subseteq A_n.
\]

Now for arbitrary \(i,j\), let \(g=\gcd(i,j)\). Since \(g\mid i\) and \(g\mid j\),

\[
A_g\subseteq A_i\cap A_j.
\]

But \(|A_g|=g\) and \(|A_i\cap A_j|=g\), so

\[
A_i\cap A_j=A_{\gcd(i,j)}.
\]

Now take an element \(x\) that appears in at least one set \(A_i\). Let \(r\) be the smallest positive integer such that \(x\in A_r\). If \(x\in A_i\), then \(x\in A_r\cap A_i=A_{\gcd(r,i)}\). Since \(\gcd(r,i)\le r\), minimality of \(r\) forces \(\gcd(r,i)=r\), so \(r\mid i\). Conversely, if \(r\mid i\), then \(A_r\subseteq A_i\), so \(x\in A_i\).

Thus each element \(x\) has a unique “root” \(r(x)\) such that

\[
x\in A_i \iff r(x)\mid i.
\]

Define

\[
C_r=\{x:\ r(x)=r\}.
\]

Then

\[
A_n=\bigcup_{r\mid n} C_r.
\]

Since \(|A_n|=n\),

\[
\sum_{r\mid n}|C_r|=n.
\]

By Möbius inversion,

\[
|C_r|=\sum_{d\mid r}\mu\left(\frac{r}{d}\right)d=\varphi(r).
\]

Conversely, if we have disjoint sets \(C_r\) with \(|C_r|=\varphi(r)\) and define

\[
A_n=\bigcup_{r\mid n}C_r,
\]

then

\[
|A_n|=\sum_{r\mid n}\varphi(r)=n
\]

and

\[
A_i\cap A_j=A_{\gcd(i,j)}.
\]

So the problem is completely equivalent to assigning disjoint sets \(C_r\) of size \(\varphi(r)\) to the positive integers.

---

## 2. Focus on divisors of \(250\)

For \(d\mid 250\),

\[
A_d=\bigcup_{m\mid d} C_m.
\]

Only the blocks \(C_m\) with \(m\mid 250\) affect the sum. The relevant \(m\) are

\[
1,2,5,10,25,50,125,250.
\]

Their sizes are

\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccccc}
m & 1 & 2 & 5 & 10 & 25 & 50 & 125 & 250\\
\hline
\varphi(m) & 1 & 1 & 4 & 4 & 20 & 20 & 100 & 100
\end{array}
\]

Their total size is

\[
1+1+4+4+20+20+100+100=250.
\]

The desired sum depends only on these eight blocks. We may assume their labels are exactly \(1,2,\dots,250\), because replacing the \(250\) relevant labels by \(1,\dots,250\) in increasing order cannot increase any maximum.

For each divisor \(d\mid 250\), let

\[
S_d=\{m\mid 250:\ m\mid d\}.
\]

Then \(\max A_d\) is the completion time of the group \(S_d\), i.e. the largest label among the blocks in \(S_d\).

---

## 3. Lower bound

Let \(M_d=\max A_d\). For \(t\in[0,250]\), let \(N(t)\) be the number of divisors \(d\mid 250\) with \(M_d\le t\). Then

\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}M_d=\int_0^{250}(8-N(t))\,dt.
\]

If \(N(t)\ge r\), then the union of the corresponding \(r\) block-sets has total size at most \(t\). Let \(W_r\) be the minimum possible total size of a union of \(r\) of the eight sets \(S_d\). Then

\[
N(t)\le h(t):=\max\{r:W_r\le t\}.
\]

The eight groups are

\[
\begin{aligned}
S_1&=\{1\},\\
S_2&=\{1,2\},\\
S_5&=\{1,5\},\\
S_{10}&=\{1,2,5,10\},\\
S_{25}&=\{1,5,25\},\\
S_{50}&=\{1,2,5,10,25,50\},\\
S_{125}&=\{1,5,25,125\},\\
S_{250}&=\{1,2,5,10,25,50,125,250\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Using the block sizes above, the minimum union sizes \(W_r\) are

\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccccc}
r & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 & 7 & 8\\
\hline
W_r & 0 & 1 & 2 & 6 & 10 & 30 & 50 & 150 & 250
\end{array}
\]

Indeed:

- \(W_1=1\), \(W_2=2\).
- To complete three groups, we need blocks \(1,2,5\), total \(6\).
- To complete four groups, we need blocks \(1,2,5,10\), total \(10\).
- A fifth group forces adding a \(20\)-block, so \(W_5=10+20=30\).
- A sixth group forces both \(20\)-blocks, so \(W_6=10+20+20=50\).
- Seven groups either include \(S_{250}\), giving \(250\), or are all the others, giving \(250-100=150\).
- \(W_8=250\).

Thus

\[
h(t)=
\begin{cases}
0,&0\le t<1,\\
1,&1\le t<2,\\
2,&2\le t<6,\\
3,&6\le t<10,\\
4,&10\le t<30,\\
5,&30\le t<50,\\
6,&50\le t<150,\\
7,&150\le t<250,\\
8,&t\ge 250.
\end{cases}
\]

Therefore

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{d\mid 250}M_d
&\ge \int_0^{250}(8-h(t))\,dt\\
&=8(1)+7(1)+6(4)+5(4)+4(20)+3(20)+2(100)+1(100)\\
&=8+7+24+20+80+60+200+100\\
&=499.
\end{aligned}
\]

So the sum is at least \(499\).

---

## 4. Construction attaining \(499\)

Define the relevant blocks as follows:

\[
\begin{aligned}
C_1&=\{1\},\\
C_2&=\{2\},\\
C_5&=\{3,4,5,6\},\\
C_{10}&=\{7,8,9,10\},\\
C_{25}&=\{11,12,\dots,30\},\\
C_{50}&=\{31,32,\dots,50\},\\
C_{125}&=\{51,52,\dots,150\},\\
C_{250}&=\{151,152,\dots,250\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

For all other \(m\nmid 250\), choose disjoint sets \(C_m\) of size \(\varphi(m)\) using positive integers larger than \(250\). Then define

\[
A_n=\bigcup_{m\mid n}C_m.
\]

This satisfies the required condition.

Now compute the maxima:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
d & \max A_d\\
\hline
1 & 1\\
2 & 2\\
5 & 6\\
10 & 10\\
25 & 30\\
50 & 50\\
125 & 150\\
250 & 250
\end{array}
\]

Hence

\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}\max A_d
=1+2+6+10+30+50+150+250
=499.
\]

Thus the minimum possible value is

\[
\boxed{499}
\]
